newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
AUSTRALIA WILL BE AT THE AMERICA'S CUP
Australia will certainly challenge New Zealand for the America's Cup in Auckland in 2000, possibly with two syndicates, one headed by SYD FISCHER, the other involving DENNIS O'NEIL and IAIN MURRAY.

FISCHER told me today he was considering lodging a late challenge (May 14 is the deadline) with the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron, either with the yacht he used at San Diego in 1995, obviously to be updated, or with a new boat.
"We have not yet made a decision...we are looking at it...but we have until May," the veteran yachtsman said.
If he does challenge, FISCHER will equal the record of Sir THOMAS LIPTON'S five attempts to win the Cup.

FISCHER also confirmed he will charter a brand new Bruce Farr designed IMS yacht, about a 50-footer, for the Admiral's Cup at Cowes, England, in July/August, rather than use one of his existing Ragamuffin 50-footers.

As we reported exclusively last week, the Gazebo Hotels boss will captain a team comprising Sydney advertising man STEVE KULMAR with a Mumm 36 one-design yacht and a syndicate headed by Melbourne merchant banker JOHN CALVERT-JONES campaigning a chartered ILC 40.
O'NEIL/MURRAY CHALLENGE LIKELY

Back to the America's Cup and the second possible challenge. Neither DENNIS O'NEIL nor IAIN MURRAY were available for comment today but it's a logical combination as the two are closely involved in some major property development projects and have mutual yachting interests.

MURRAY may well be remembered as the skipper of Kookaburra which lost the America's Cup to DENNIS CONNER off Fremantle in 1987, and as one of the design team of JOHN BERTRAND'S sinkable oneAUSTRALIA for the San Diego challenge in 1995.

Since then he has concentrated on designing ocean racing yachts and sports boats, the results showing he is an outstanding and innovative yacht designer with the capability to design an America's Cup boat. MURRAY has had outstanding success with his ocean racing IMS designs and a logical move would be to build an America's Cup challenger at the Bashford International operation at Nowra on the NSW Coast recently acquired by a group involving MURRAY and Capital Investments chairman CHARLES CURRAN.

O'NEIL, who has widely varied business interests in Sydney, has always been an active yachting enthusiast. He has represented Australia three times at the Admiral's Cup, with Koomooloo in 1969 and 1971 when the Australian team placed second and third, and again in 1983 with Bondi Tram, with the team placing fourth that year.

He was also an active Soling sailor as a young man, sailing with the 1972 Star class Gold medallists DAVID FORBES and JOHN ANDERSON in the Montreal Games in 1976 where the yachting was held on Lake Ontario off Kingston.
MILSON CUP WIN TO NINETY SEVEN

Boutique resort hotel owner and Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron member ANDREW STRACHAN made a welcome return to the winner's circle last weekend when he skippered his duck-egg blue 47-footer, Ninety Seven, to victory in the Milson Cup.

The Milson Cup, which commemorates one of the founding members of the Squadron, is regarded as one of the great traditional trophy events on the offshore calendar, last weekend attracting some 60 entries.

Ninety Seven, the Farr 47 which survived the gale of 1993 to become the smallest yacht in 40 years to take line honours in the Sydney-to-Hobart, was the first casualty of the recent race to Hobart -- the ham in the sandwich in a starting collision.

STRACHAN, who owns the up-market Kims Resort at Toowoon Bay on the NSW Central Coast, was certainly in a far greater champagne cork-popping mood last Saturday evening than he was back at the CYCA on Boxing Day. Among the yachts he beat was SYD FISCHER'S champion 50-footer, Ragamuffin.
Line honours in the short ocean triangle went to Infinity III, the Farr 66 which also is having a new lease of life under the ownership of Sydney solicitor MARTIN JAMES.
GILMOUR MISSES OUT ON AUSTRALIA CUP

PETER GILMOUR had to be content with third place in a dramatic Australia Cup international match racing series sailed on the Swan River at Perth last week, but his performance has still lifted him into second place in International Sailing Federation's Omega world rankings.

GILMOUR, sailing with an all-Japanese crew as part of his agreement to skipper the Japanese challenger for the America s Cup in 2000, sailed a fine lead-up series to finish equal top of the scoreboard after two round-robins of match racing.

But in the semi-finals, he lost to Britain's CHRIS LAW who went on to win the Australia Cup in a hard-fought against France's THIERRY PEPONNET. GILMOUR beat Sweden's MAGNUS HOLMBERG in the sail-off for third berth, that placing lifting him into second place in world standings, with New Zealand's RUSSELL COUTTS still on top.

While GILMOUR'S aggressive sailing skills in match racing have been lost to Japan for the next America's Cup, he is maintaining close links with Australia and on Monday evening at the Hotel Nikko he will launch what the invitation describes as an exciting new business and sporting venture between Australia and Japan.
ADELAIDE TO PORT LINCOLN OCEAN RACE

South Australia's major ocean race of the year, from Adelaide to Port Lincoln, starts from Outer Harbour today with a fleet that exceeds that of the recent Sydney-to-Hobart and includes some of Australia's best ocean racing yachts.

This will be the 47th annual Lincoln race conducted by the Royal South Australian Yacht Squadron and the club's manager DAVID HARRIES expects a fleet of more than 100 yachts to set sail on the 172 nautical mile Fosters Bluewater Classic.
The Cruising Division, which includes a contingent of some 30 boats from Victoria, set sail at 10am while the Racing Division will start at 3pm.
Among the top local IMS yachts competing are GEOFF BOETTCHER's new MURRAY-designed 41-footer, Secret Mens Business, GEOFF VERCOE'S Maglieri Wines, and GRAHAM WILLIAMS' Prime Example.
Victorian entries include the Melbourne to Hobart race record-holder PL Lend Lease Future Shock (PETER HANSEN) and the handicap winner of that race, THORRY GUNNERSEN'S Tilting at Windmills.
One to watch will be Melbourne sailmaker ROSS LLOYD, sailing master aboard the Sydney-to-Hobart overall IMS winner, Ausmaid, who will be sailing his own Bull 9000 one-designer race to Port Lincoln.
The race record stands at 15 hours 33 minutes set in 1995 by veteran Adelaide yachtsman KEITH FLINT in his famous pocket maxi HELSAL II, competing again this year.
The race to Port Lincoln will be followed by the popular Lincoln Week Regatta next week which includes the strong local fleet of Etchells and other classes.
* Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800.
